transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hello, doctor. Lately I keep forgetting everyday things I’m supposed to do, like taking my pills or bringing what I need to church events, even when I write them down. It’s been really embarrassing for me because I’ve always prided myself on being reliable, but I just can't seem to keep track of things anymore.
Along with these memory struggles, have you also been feeling persistently down, sad, or lost interest in the activities you normally enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I'm feeling down or losing interest in my activities, as I actually still love being involved in everything. I'm just feeling really frustrated and embarrassed by these memory slips and how hard it's become to keep up with all the things I want to do.
Are you still able to manage your daily activities, like handling your finances, cooking, or taking care of your home, completely on your own, or do you now need help from others?

I still manage basic things on my own, like cooking and straightening up the house. However, I really struggle with daily tasks like remembering my pills, and my daughter has actually started double-checking my schedule because I keep mixing up dates.
Would you say you are still able to live and manage your daily life independently, even if it takes more effort, or do you now depend on others to get through the day safely?

I can absolutely still live independently and manage on my own, though it takes a great deal of extra effort and I've had some setbacks. I don't need help to live safely, but my daughter has started double-checking my plans because she's worried I'll drop the ball with the grandkids' schedules. Sadly, people at church and my volunteer groups have also stopped relying on me for important tasks because of these mix-ups.
Have you recently been diagnosed with any medical conditions, or did you experience any physical illnesses, infections, or head injuries around the time these memory issues started?
No, I haven't had any new medical diagnoses or physical illnesses lately. I also haven't had any head injuries or infections around the time these issues started.
Do you have any long-standing chronic medical conditions, such as high blood pressure, diabetes, or thyroid issues, even if you've been treating them for a long time?

To my knowledge, I don't have any major chronic conditions like high blood pressure, diabetes, or thyroid issues. I really just take some daily vitamins and supplements for my general health. Though, as I mentioned, those are some of the pills I keep forgetting to take!
Besides your memory, have you noticed other changes, like having trouble finding the right words when speaking, getting confused about the date or time, or getting lost in places you know well?

No, I don't have any trouble finding my words, and I never get confused about the date or get lost in familiar places. My struggles are strictly with keeping track of my daily tasks and staying focused on what I'm supposed to be doing.
Have you ever been told by a doctor that you experienced a mini-stroke (TIA), a silent stroke, or any other brain-related condition in the past?
No, I have never been told anything like that. I've never had a mini-stroke, a silent stroke, or any other kind of brain-related condition.
How long have you been experiencing these memory slips and difficulties keeping track of your schedule?

These difficulties have been steadily getting in the way for almost two years now. It really started becoming a major problem after my husband passed away and I retired, which left my days feeling much more unstructured.
You mentioned having trouble with your schedule and pills, but are you still able to handle complex tasks like managing your finances and paying bills entirely on your own?
I haven't really had any major issues with managing my finances or paying my bills. I still handle those tasks on my own, so I haven't thought about it much as being a problem.
Have you had any medical tests, such as brain scans or blood work, specifically to investigate these memory issues since they started?
No, I haven't had any brain scans or specific blood work done for these issues. My primary care doctor simply referred me for this psychiatric evaluation after I brought up my difficulties to him.
Have these memory and scheduling difficulties been gradually getting worse over the past two years, or have they remained at about the same level of severity?

They have gradually become more of a constant, frustrating problem over the last two years. It started becoming much more noticeable after my husband passed and I retired, and as I took on more volunteer projects with unstructured time, keeping track of everything just got harder.
Have you or your family noticed any changes in your ability to make decisions, solve everyday problems, or use good judgment?

No, my family and I haven't really noticed any issues with my decision-making, problem-solving, or judgment itself. My main struggle is simply keeping track of details, remembering to do things, and staying focused, rather than making poor choices.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a two-year history of gradual cognitive decline, primarily affecting memory and executive function (scheduling and tracking tasks). While these difficulties cause her frustration and have led to some social setbacks (e.g., peers at church relying on her less), she remains fully independent in her activities of daily living, such as cooking, housekeeping, and managing her finances, though requiring compensatory strategies and extra effort. The preservation of independence in daily functioning rules out dementia (F03) and aligns with Mild Cognitive Disorder (F06.7).
